content:
watchOS 27 is coming soon, and it's the next major software update for Apple Watch. I've been testing the watchOS 27 beta this summer, and there are three new features that I especially like.

#1: New Home Screen View

In my view, Apple has never really nailed the watchOS home screen. The original honeycomb design looks great in promotional images, and the list view added later was my go-to, but both ways feel a bit awkward.

The problem is that Apple Watch is designed for very brief micro-interactions. And watchOS comes preloaded with tons of apps—plus all the third-party ones added on top—to have to scroll through a bunch of apps you never use just to find the one you want is really annoying.

watchOS 27 offers a solution: a dynamic app grid, which has become the new default home screen view.

The dynamic app grid is similar to the honeycomb-style "grid view," but it only shows your five most frequently used apps plus the Siri app. In my experience, it almost always shows the apps I want to use. If it really doesn't, you can still opt to open the full app view.

Most of the time, the complications on my watch face are my primary way to launch apps. But now the dynamic app grid has become a handy secondary option.

#2: Tap Gesture

Over the past few years, Apple has gradually added various novel and interesting gesture controls.

Double Tap was the first gesture to launch, and Wrist Flick was added last year.

Now watchOS 27 adds a third option: Tap. It's like Double Tap, but just a single tap, and it only works with Smart Stack.

When browsing Smart Stack, a light tap with your index finger and thumb will select the highlighted widget. Basically it's a handy selection tool.

Now you can open Smart Stack and use Double Tap to browse, then use the new Tap gesture to select a widget and open the corresponding app.

#3: Siri AI

Siri AI is at the heart of all of Apple's new software this fall, and watchOS 27 is no exception.

Apple rebuilt Siri from the ground up for the AI era, which is a huge upgrade compared to before.

watchOS 27 adds a dedicated Siri app, letting you browse your conversation history with the assistant across all your devices. Importantly, the Apple Watch version of Siri isn't some watered-down, stripped-to-the-bone version made for the wrist—it's the exact same Siri AI as on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other devices.

According to Apple's senior director of watchOS software engineering (via TechRadar), that's exactly one of the goals of this Siri overhaul:

As companies race to develop successful AI wearables, watchOS 27 will make the already hugely popular Apple Watch one of them.

Which features of watchOS 27 do you like? Drop a comment and let us know.
